y-m-03-01.title: Same row of buttons, different groups of big buttons
y-m-03-01.topic: Sorting standards: choosing words wey dey give everybody di same result
y-m-03-01.goal: Understand say sorting with word like 'big', wey boundary no clear, fit give different results for different people. Make and explain standard wey go give di same result no matter who dey sort.
y-m-03-01.material:
8 buttons dey line up in one row from di smallest to di biggest. From left dem name 가, 나, 다, 라, 마, 바, 사, and 아. All di buttons get di same color and shape; na only their size different.
Mina gather 라, 마, 바, 사, and 아 (5 buttons) as 'big buttons'. Hajun gather 마, 바, 사, and 아 (4 buttons) as 'big buttons'. Both look the same row of buttons, and both sort dem using di words 'big button'.
y-m-03-01.thinking.1: Judge wetin else dem need to get di same result
y-m-03-01.thinking.2: Make clear sorting standard by yourself
y-m-03-01.prereq.0: Sorting things according to one standard
y-m-03-01.s.s1.prompt: Which reason best explain why di big buttons wey di two people gather different?
y-m-03-01.s.s1.hint.0: Write di big buttons wey di two people gather side by side and find which buttons different.
y-m-03-01.s.s1.hint.1: Think whether to put dat button inside 'big buttons' or not, and if na you dey decide, wetin you go look to decide.
y-m-03-01.s.s1.o.a: Mina eye better than Hajun own, so Mina grouping more correct
y-m-03-01.s.s1.r.a: You see am as question of good or bad eyesight. Both people look di same row and group using word 'big', so di difference na where di word boundary dey.
y-m-03-01.s.s1.o.b: Dem count di number wrong, so if dem count again, di two people result go be the same
y-m-03-01.s.s1.r.b: You see am as counting mistake. Di difference between 5 and 4 fit come from counting mistake, but e fit also be because dem disagree where to start calling button 'big'.
y-m-03-01.s.s1.o.c: Hajun no know wetin 'big' mean, so na only Hajun wrong and Mina correct
y-m-03-01.s.s1.r.c: You see am as only one person wrong. Both people group consistently using their own standard.
y-m-03-01.s.s1.o.d: Di word alone no settle which button 'big' start from, so dem draw di boundary differently
y-m-03-01.s.s1.r.d: You focus on where di word 'big' divide dem. Dis thinking examine di boundary of di word wey serve as standard.
y-m-03-01.s.s1.explain: With only word like 'big', wey people fit draw di boundary differently, e hard to get same result. Mina see buttons from 라 upward as 'big buttons', and Hajun see buttons from 마 upward as 'big'. Both sort consistently using their own standard.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.prompt: For di two people to get di same result from now on, wetin dem must decide first?
y-m-03-01.s.s2.hint.0: Point again to where Mina and Hajun sort differently.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.hint.1: Think wetin di two people need to agree on so dem go decide the same way which side to put am for dat point.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.o.a: Make di two people decide with di same method which button to count as 'big button' from
y-m-03-01.s.s2.r.a: You focus on where di dividing line dey. You choose wetin dem need to make di standard one.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.o.b: Instead of 'big button', call am stronger word like 'very big button'
y-m-03-01.s.s2.r.b: People fit still see differently where 'very big' start. If you only change di word, di boundary still no settle.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.o.c: Compare di results wey di two people group and follow di one wey get bigger count
y-m-03-01.s.s2.r.c: Dis row don get one settled result, but for other rows of buttons, e fit different again. E no settle wetin 'big' mean.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.o.d: One person group first and di other one follow
y-m-03-01.s.s2.r.d: You think about di order of grouping. If you group by following, you only copy one person's boundary, and di standard no settle.
y-m-03-01.s.s2.explain: Once dem decide which button from there count as 'big button', di dividing line don settle as one. Plenty ways dey to decide am (for example, from button 라, or bigger than di middle button).
y-m-03-01.s.s3.prompt: Make and write new way to explain how to sort 'big buttons' so di same result go come out no matter who dey sort. Add few words about why di same result go come out.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.hint.0: First decide which button name (가 to 아) to use as di boundary.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.hint.1: Read wetin you write to friend and imagine whether di same buttons go come out.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: With di words wey you decide, e don settle which buttons be big buttons?
y-m-03-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: If Mina and Hajun read wetin I write, dem go choose same buttons?
y-m-03-01.s.s3.model.0: If you decide say buttons from 라 upward na big buttons, di same result go come out no matter who sort.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.model.1: If you talk 'bigger than button 마', Mina and Hajun go sort exactly di same way.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.model.2: Call button big if e bigger than di middle button. Di cut point don settle, so everybody go get di same result.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.modelNote.2: If di row get two middle buttons, you need decide one more time, like 'di left one of di two middle buttons'.
y-m-03-01.s.s3.model.3: If you call any button at least two times as big as di smallest button a big button and group dem by measuring with ruler, di same result go come out no matter who group.

y-m-03-02.title: I split dem into two boxes, but di cards increase
y-m-03-02.topic: Looking at overlap and gaps in sorting results
y-m-03-02.goal: Understand say if names of sorted boxes overlap or some cards no fit any box, di counted result fit different from total. Fix di sorting so every card go to exactly one place.
y-m-03-02.material:
Altogether, 9 cards dey. Di card names and number of cards be like dis.
[Cards] Red circle 3 cards / Blue circle 2 cards / Red triangle 2 cards / Blue triangle 2 cards (total 9 cards)
Seoa make two boxes. One na 'red card box' and di other na 'circle card box'. She look cards one by one and put each card wey fit one box inside am. Cards wey no fit any box remain for desk.
y-m-03-02.thinking.0: Finding statement wey no get reason for solution
y-m-03-02.thinking.1: Checking whether sorting names dey overlap
y-m-03-02.thinking.2: Comparing several ways to fix am
y-m-03-02.prereq.0: Sorting and counting things by color or shape
y-m-03-02.s.s1.prompt: Na Seoa thinking be dis. Choose di line wey get one place wey hard to trust.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.hint.0: Pick one red circle card and check one by one which of di two boxes e fit enter.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.hint.1: Separate cards for boxes from cards wey remain for desk and write number of cards for each.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.line.1: Red card box get 5 cards and circle card box get 5 cards.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.line.2: 5 and 5 together make 10, so 10 cards dey inside di boxes.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.line.3: 10 cards dey for boxes, so na 10 cards, no be 9.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.line.4: I split dem into two boxes and no card remain outside, so di sorting good.
y-m-03-02.s.s1.explain: Line 3: di 3 red circles fit both 'red card box' and 'circle card box', so dem count am twice. So 10, di sum of 5 and 5, no be di number of cards. Line 4: di increase to 10 cards wey dem count for boxes happen because dem count same cards two times. E no mean say di 9 cards wey dem count at first wrong. Line 5: di 2 blue triangles no fit enter any box, so dem remain for desk. So 'without leaving any outside' no correct too. Lines 1 and 2 talk di counted result as e be, so dem fine.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.prompt: Choose all di ways to fix am so every card go enter only one box.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.hint.0: Write di two box names side by side and look for cards wey fit both names.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.hint.1: For each fixed box, mark how many times each of di four kinds of cards enter.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.o.a: Divide into two boxes: circle cards and triangle cards
y-m-03-02.s.s2.r.a: You make two boxes using one standard (shape) and check say every card enter only one place.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.o.b: Divide into three boxes: red cards, circle cards, triangle cards
y-m-03-02.s.s2.r.b: You think say making more boxes go solve am. Even among di three boxes, red circle fit enter two places, 'red' and 'circle'.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.o.c: Remove di 2 blue triangle cards without counting dem
y-m-03-02.s.s2.r.c: You try to make di sum match by removing cards wey no fit. If you remove dem, you no classify di cards, you only reduce dem.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.o.d: Divide into two boxes: red cards and blue cards
y-m-03-02.s.s2.r.d: You make two boxes using di other standard (color) and check whether each card enter only one place.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.o.e: Put di 3 overlapping cards only inside red card box
y-m-03-02.s.s2.r.e: If you put overlapping cards for only one side, double counting go reduce. But di blue triangle cards still no get place.
y-m-03-02.s.s2.explain: If you make boxes using one standard (only shape or only color), every card go enter exactly one place. With shape standard, na 5 circles and 4 triangles; with color standard, na 5 red and 4 blue. Di sum na 9 cards for both.
y-m-03-02.s.s3.prompt: Woojin talk, 'Red circle fit enter both boxes, so we fit use di first way as e be.' How you go answer Woojin? Use red circle cards as example and write numbers.
y-m-03-02.s.s3.hint.0: Count and write how many times di 3 red circle cards enter which box.
y-m-03-02.s.s3.hint.1: Put di number of cards for both boxes and total number of cards side by side and compare.
y-m-03-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: From di numbers wey you write, e clear say 5+5=10 different from 9 cards?
y-m-03-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Your reason why dem no suppose use di first method as e be include words like 'counted twice'?
y-m-03-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: E include at least one way to fix am too?
y-m-03-02.s.s3.model.0: Di 3 red circles enter both red box and circle box, so dem count am twice. So e become 5+5=10, wey different from di 9 cards.
y-m-03-02.s.s3.model.1: You gatz divide by only one thing. Di red circles enter both boxes, so dem overlap. If you divide only by shape, e be 5 circles and 4 triangles, so di sum na 9 cards.

y-m-03-03.title: Can one group table tell about di whole class?
y-m-03-03.topic: Di range wey di data collect fit tell us: one group and di whole class
y-m-03-03.goal: Understand say survey results from only some friends no fit settle wetin di whole class think. Talk wetin else you need to know, and change your statement when more data dey collected.
y-m-03-03.material:
Our class get 20 students, in 4 groups of 5. We decide say each person go choose one favorite snack and we go survey each group. Right now, na only Group 1 result come out.
[Group 1] Tteokbokki 3 students / Snacks 1 student / Fruit 1 student (total 5 students)
Doyun talk, "Di snack wey our class like pass na tteokbokki!"
y-m-03-03.thinking.0: Judge di range wey di data tell us
y-m-03-03.thinking.1: Judge whether di information plenty and talk di information wey you need
y-m-03-03.thinking.2: Use new data fix di first statement
y-m-03-03.prereq.0: Counting data by type and reading table
y-m-03-03.prereq.1: Comparing sizes of numbers up to 20
y-m-03-03.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about wetin Doyun talk, based only on dis table?
y-m-03-03.s.s1.hint.0: Count how many students' results dey in di table, and write am next to number of students in whole class.
y-m-03-03.s.s1.hint.1: Looking at di table, write in two lines wetin you fit say for sure and wetin you still no know.
y-m-03-03.s.s1.o.a: For Group 1, tteokbokki plenty pass, but we still no know about di whole class
y-m-03-03.s.s1.r.a: You separate wetin di table tell (Group 1) from wetin we still no know (di whole class).
y-m-03-03.s.s1.o.b: You fit say tteokbokki na di most popular for di whole class too
y-m-03-03.s.s1.r.b: You carry result of 5 people straight over to result of all 20. You never see result of di other 15 yet.
y-m-03-03.s.s1.o.c: Only 5 students dey, so this table no tell anything
y-m-03-03.s.s1.r.c: You think data useless because small. But within Group 1, tteokbokki most popular.
y-m-03-03.s.s1.o.d: Snack and fruit with 1 student each fit count as nothing
y-m-03-03.s.s1.r.d: You treat small counts as zero. Even 1 student na person's choice, gats count.
y-m-03-03.s.s1.explain: This table show result for 5 students in Group 1. We never know results for other 15 of 20 classmates. You fit say tteokbokki most popular inside Group 1.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.prompt: To say which snack whole class like best, choose all info you still need.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.hint.0: Write difference between number of people you know now and people you wan know.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.hint.1: Think one by one whether each choice change "count for a snack."
y-m-03-03.s.s2.o.a: How much one bowl of tteokbokki cost
y-m-03-03.s.s2.r.a: You focus on price. Price no affect which snack more people choose.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.o.b: Snacks wey 15 people in other 3 groups choose
y-m-03-03.s.s2.r.b: You check say you need results of friends you never see yet.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.o.c: Whether any friend in other groups miss the survey
y-m-03-03.s.s2.r.c: You check if all 15 join survey. If anyone missing, hard to call am whole-class result.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.r.d: You focus on names. Names no change how many people choose each snack.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.explain: To talk about whole class, you need results of other 15 students, and check whether each person choose only one thing so counts add up to 20.
y-m-03-03.s.s2.acc.0: Most important na result for other 15. Good to check nobody left out when collecting answers.
y-m-03-03.s.s3.prompt:

[Group 2] Tteokbokki 1 student / Snacks 3 students / Fruit 1 student
[Group 3] Tteokbokki 1 student / Snacks 3 students / Fruit 1 student
[Group 4] Tteokbokki 2 students / Snacks 1 student / Fruit 2 students

y-m-03-03.s.s3.hint.0: Write which snack most popular in Group 1 result and four-group result, compare.
y-m-03-03.s.s3.hint.1: Write difference in students between snacks and tteokbokki, and how to describe am.
y-m-03-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: The 8 and 7 you write same as table numbers?
y-m-03-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write difference between what you say from Group 1 and four groups?
y-m-03-03.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You think how to say 8 and 7 differ by 1 student?

y-m-03-03.s.s3.model.1: Snacks get 8, tteokbokki 7, difference na 1. Snacks most, but almost same, so good to say many people like tteokbokki too.

y-m-03-06.title: If row long, e mean more cards?

y-m-03-06.material:

y-m-03-06.s.s1.r.b: You decide only because cards close. Touching no prove more cards.

y-m-03-09.title: If one friend change mind, will result change?

y-m-03-08.title: I want table like this: make table fit conditions
y-m-03-08.topic: Make survey table with conditions and what table fit show
y-m-03-08.goal: Make several tables meeting sum and order conditions; distinguish what table tell for sure from wetin no fit tell.
y-m-03-08.material:

Condition 3: zoo count > amusement park > museum.
